purpose: Read-only repository case studies for the proposed music-theory-production-engineering skill and its charters (music-theory-research-director, audio-dsp-production-engineer, creative-rights-reproducibility-editor). Records verified license posture, pinned commit, lifecycle, and license/lifecycle/path lessons. No code was downloaded or executed; inspection via GitHub API (license endpoint + raw LICENSE file reads + commit listing) on 2026-11-21.
verification: Same protocol as civilization_design_repo_cases.json. License choices matter doubly in audio: copyleft engines (Csound LGPL-2.1, SuperCollider GPL-3.0, Essentia AGPL-3.0, pedalboard GPL-3.0) impose different obligations than permissive libraries (Tone.js MIT, music21 BSD-3-Clause, librosa ISC, mir_eval MIT) — this is a product-architecture input, recorded per case.

cases.name: Tonejs/Tone.js
cases.demonstrates: Web Audio scheduling and graph abstraction for the browser: transport/lookahead scheduling, synth/effect units; reference for lab M2.
implementation_lessons: AudioContext sample-accurate timing comes from the Web Audio clock, not setTimeout — Tone.Transport exists precisely because naive JS scheduling drifts.
MIT posture makes it safe for commercial web deliverables; still record version pin + NOTICE.
Version cadence is high: pin exact version (v15.x) in lab fixtures, and declare AudioContext sample rate in every test.

cases.name: WebAudio/web-audio-api

license.spdx: W3C Software and Document License (GitHub: NOASSERTION)
license.how_verified: LICENSE.md read — 'All documents in this Repository are licensed by contributors under the W3C Software and Document License'

lifecycle.status: active — v1.1-era maintenance (errata like coneGain vector fix observed)

cases.demonstrates: The normative browser audio graph API (nodes, AudioWorklet, automation timelines) maintained as inspectable spec text with public issue discussion.
implementation_lessons: Quote API behavior by spec version + section; errata land between formal publications — the repo is the living document.
AudioWorklet runs off the main thread: messaging latency and 128-frame render quantum belong in lab acceptance tests.
Spec issues are public: implementation conformance differs across browsers — test, don't assume.

cases.name: w3c/musicxml

license.spdx: no repo-level LICENSE file (verified at root listing 2026-11-21); governed by W3C Music Notation Community Group agreements — treat spec text under W3C document terms and record this when excerpting

cases.demonstrates: The interchange format for Western notation between notation editors, analysis tools, and renderers; XSD schema in-repo makes validation teachable (lab M3).
implementation_lessons: Interchange ≠ semantics: MusicXML carries notation and much performance data, but round-trips through different editors can alter layout/voice assignment — acceptance-test the musical content, not the file hash.
Origins: Michael Good / Recordare → MakeMusic → donated to the W3C CG (2015); a licensing-governance example of a de facto standard moving to a standards body.
Absence of repo LICENSE is a finding: cite the CG page and W3C terms, not an assumed open license.

cases.name: cuthbertLab/music21

lifecycle.status: active — long-lived academic project (copyright 2006–2026 per LICENSE)

cases.demonstrates: Symbolic music analysis in Python: streams/parts/measures, corpus of encoded works, Roman-numeral and species-counterpoint tooling; the workhorse for harmony/counterpoint verification in labs.
implementation_lessons: The bundled corpus has its own rights posture — scores encoded from editions may carry edition rights; check before redistributing derived encodings.
Analytical output is a hypothesis about a score, not a property of it: report method (e.g., key-finding algorithm + parameters) with every analysis.
BSD posture + active maintainer makes it a safe default dependency; pin major version (v9+ API changes exist historically).

cases.name: musescore/MuseScore

license.spdx: GPL-3.0 with font exception (bundled fonts under GNU Freefont with embedding exception)

cases.demonstrates: Full engraving application with headless CLI (batch convert MusicXML→PDF/PNG/audio): reference renderer for lab M3 fixtures; also the font-exception pattern that keeps document embedding unencumbered.
implementation_lessons: GPL-3.0 governs the application; scores you author are your works (output is not a derivative of the program), and the font exception explicitly keeps embedded-font documents non-GPL — quote this distinction in rights reviews.
Headless conversion is version-sensitive: pin MuseScore version for reproducible rendering fixtures.
musescore.com (the sharing platform) has separate terms from the GPL application — never conflate the two in rights discussions.

cases.name: csound/csound
cases.demonstrates: Composer-programmer synthesis language with decades of documented opcodes; embeddable engine (Csound API) used inside games, mobile apps, and plugins.
implementation_lessons: LGPL-2.1 permits embedding via dynamic linking in proprietary hosts; static-link or engine modifications trigger source obligations — architecture decision to record.
Orchestra/score text files are inspectable artifacts: ideal for reproducible synthesis labs (seed + sr + ksmps declared).
Opcode numerical behavior can differ across versions/platforms; acceptance tests must declare sample rate and control-rate.

cases.name: supercollider/supercollider
cases.demonstrates: scsynth server + sclang client architecture (OSC protocol between them): the canonical client/server live-coding and generative-audio engine.
implementation_lessons: GPL-3.0 is strong copyleft: distributing sclang/scsynth derivatives (including some plugin-bundled apps) carries source obligations; scsynth's OSC interface lets GPL engine and proprietary client coexist across a protocol boundary — a recurring licensing pattern.
Server/client split demonstrates protocol-based isolation for both latency and license reasons.
UGen graph state is process-local: reproducibility requires scd source + version + seed, never just a bounced file.

cases.name: MTG/essentia

license.spdx: AGPL-3.0 (with upstream contribution terms; also historically available under commercial license from UPF)

lifecycle.status: active (Universitat Pompeu Fabra Music Technology Group)

cases.demonstrates: Industrial-strength MIR feature extraction and inference (incl. ONNX model zoo): reference algorithms for tonal/rhythm/timbre descriptors (Bogdanov et al., ACM MM 2013).
implementation_lessons: AGPL-3.0 extends copyleft to network use: a SaaS calling Essentia must offer source — this single fact changes product architecture; permissive alternative for closed products is librosa.
Pretrained model files carry their own licenses separate from the code license — check per model before shipping.
Descriptor definitions are versioned algorithms: cite Essentia version + algorithm parameters in MIR reports.

cases.name: librosa/librosa
cases.demonstrates: The permissive Python MIR baseline (McFee et al., SciPy 2015): spectral features, onset/beat/tempo, CQT/chroma; teaching reference for MIR labs.
implementation_lessons: ISC posture makes it the safe default when AGPL/GPL engines are excluded; state this choice explicitly in architecture notes.
Defaults matter (hop length, n_fft, centering): feature comparability across studies requires declaring them — reproducibility contract §17.
NumPy/SciPy version drift changes numerics at the margins; pin the environment for benchmark fixtures.

cases.name: craffel/mir_eval

license.how_verified: LICENSE.txt read (file SHA ae0c0b8eb2b3ac302264f925c4c58892c7759722); note GitHub's license API returned null for this repo — file inspection beats API detection

pinned_commit.note: packaging modernization to pyproject; mir_eval.separation module removed in 0.9.0dev — API-surface lesson

cases.demonstrates: Transparent reference implementations of MIR metrics (Raffel et al., ISMIR 2014): the citation unit for 'how was this score computed' in every MIR claim.
implementation_lessons: Metrics have definitions with parameters (tolerance windows etc.): report metric + parameterization, never a bare number.
Module removal in a minor version (separation, load_wav) shows even slow libraries break APIs — pin versions and read changelogs.
License-file presence did not register in GitHub's API: verification protocol must include file reads, not just the API.

cases.name: 0xfe/vexflow

license.spdx: MIT text (GitHub: NOASSERTION due to header wording)
license.how_verified: LICENSE read via license API — verbatim MIT permission text

lifecycle.status: slow/maintenance — last default-branch commit 2025-03; SMuFL-based rendering mature

cases.demonstrates: Browser notation engraving with SMuFL fonts: the render layer for web notation labs and education apps (used widely, e.g., in practice platforms).
implementation_lessons: Slow commit cadence + heavy downstream use = pin version and treat as stable dependency; do not assume active security patching.
Rendering correctness is font-dependent (SMuFL metadata): declare font + version in fixtures.
NOASSERTION again resolved by file read — third instance confirming the protocol.

cases.name: surge-synthesizer/tuning-library

pinned_commit.note: bugfix + added ASAN/UBSAN CI — memory-safety practice lesson

lifecycle.status: active — maintained by the Surge Synth Team (open-source synth organization)

cases.demonstrates: Maintained C++ implementation of Scala .scl/.kbm microtuning formats: the practical bridge from tuning theory (§12) to instruments; used across the open synth ecosystem.
implementation_lessons: Tuning data is data: keyboard mapping (.kbm) vs. scale (.scl) separation is the teaching point for 'reference pitch + map' discipline.
The recent ASAN/UBSAN addition models the memory-safety bar for audio code handling untrusted files (user-supplied .scl files are untrusted input).
MIT posture enables embedding in commercial synths — the ecosystem's reason for choosing it.

cases.name: spotify/pedalboard
cases.demonstrates: Pythonic audio effects over JUCE internals, with VST3/AU plugin loading: deterministic offline processing for dataset augmentation and QC pipelines.
implementation_lessons: GPL-3.0 (chosen because JUCE modules used under GPL) propagates: including pedalboard in a distributed product or internal tooling that is conveyed triggers copyleft — record before adoption.
Loading third-party VST3 plugins inherits each plugin's license — plugin wrappers do not launder proprietary terms.
Offline render APIs make bit-exact regression tests possible: freeze parameters, buffer size, and sample rate in the fixture.
